directAnswer: Pope Benedict XII was Jacques Fournier, a Cistercian monk and former bishop of Pamiers, who reigned at Avignon from 20 December 1334 to 25 April 1342. He issued the constitution Benedictus Deus defining that the souls of the just see God immediately after death and purification, reformed the religious orders, and opposed nepotism.

sections.h2: The White Cardinal from the County of Foix
paras: Jacques Fournier was born at Saverdun in the county of Foix and became a Cistercian monk, studying theology in Paris and later serving as abbot of Fontfroide. As bishop of Pamiers from 1317, he personally conducted a detailed inquisition into Cathar beliefs in his diocese. The register of those interrogations survives and is a rich source for the daily life of medieval villagers, especially in the village of Montaillou.

John XXII made him bishop of Mirepoix and then cardinal in 1327. Because he kept wearing his white Cistercian habit, he was known as the White Cardinal. He served as a leading theologian in the curia and helped prepare the response to John XXII's beatific vision sermons.

Elected on 20 December 1334, Benedict moved quickly to resolve the controversy his predecessor had raised. In the constitution Benedictus Deus, issued in January 1336, he defined that the souls of the saints and of the faithful who need no further purification, or who have completed it, see the divine essence face to face immediately after death, without waiting for the resurrection of the body.
The constitution also taught that those who die in mortal sin go down to hell immediately. Benedictus Deus remains a basic text of Catholic teaching on the last things.

sections.h2: Reforming Monks, Friars and the Curia
paras: A monk himself, Benedict issued reform constitutions for several orders: for the Cistercians in 1335, for the Benedictines in 1336 in a document often called the Benedictina, for the Franciscans in 1336, and for the canons regular in 1339. These addressed discipline, finances and the education of members.

He sent clergy who lingered at Avignon seeking favors back to their dioceses, tightened procedures for granting benefices, and refused to advance his relatives, a marked contrast with other popes of the period.

Benedict considered returning to Rome and spent money repairing St. Peter's and the Lateran, but war in Italy and the tensions that led to the Hundred Years' War kept him in Avignon. He began building the fortress-like Palace of the Popes there, the section now called the Old Palace.
His efforts to make peace between France and England did not succeed, and his attempts at reconciliation with Louis of Bavaria failed. He died at Avignon on 25 April 1342.

keyFacts: Born Jacques Fournier at Saverdun; Cistercian monk
As bishop of Pamiers, kept the inquisition register that documents Montaillou
Issued Benedictus Deus on the beatific vision (1336)
Wrote reform constitutions for Cistercians, Benedictines, Franciscans and canons regular
Began the Palace of the Popes at Avignon

faqs.question: What did Benedictus Deus define?
faqs.answer: It defined that the souls of the just who have no need of purification, or who have been purified, see God face to face immediately after death, before the final resurrection.

faqs.question: What is the Fournier Register?
faqs.answer: It is the record of the inquisition Jacques Fournier conducted as bishop of Pamiers in the 1310s and 1320s. Its detailed testimonies, especially from Montaillou, are valued by historians of medieval daily life.

faqs.question: Why was Benedict XII called the White Cardinal?
faqs.answer: As a Cistercian he continued to wear the order's white habit after being made a cardinal in 1327.
